title: Mutation-Guided Unit Test Generation with a Large Language Model
authors: Guancheng Wang, Qinghua Xu, Lionel C. Briand, Kui Liu
abstract: This paper proposes MutGen, a mutation-guided, LLM-based test generation approach that incorporates mutation feedback directly into the prompt that significantly outperforms both EvoSuite and vanilla prompt-based strategies in terms of mutation score.

title: An Empirical Evaluation of Using Large Language Models for Automated Unit Test Generation
authors: Max Schäfer, Sarah Nadi, Aryaz Eghbali, Frank Tip
abstract: A large-scale empirical evaluation on the effectiveness of large Language Models for automated unit test generation without requiring additional training or manual effort is presented.

title: CodaMosa: Escaping Coverage Plateaus in Test Generation with Pre-trained Large Language Models
authors: Caroline Lemieux, Jeevana Priya Inala, Shuvendu K. Lahiri, Siddhartha Sen
venue: 2023 IEEE/ACM 45th International Conference on Software Engineering (ICSE)
abstract: This paper explores whether Large Language Models of code, such as OpenAI's Codex, can be used to help SBST's exploration, and proposes CodaMosa, a proposed algorithm that conducts SBST until its coverage improvements stall, then asks Codex to provide example test cases for under-covered functions.

title: Effective Test Generation Using Pre-trained Large Language Models and Mutation Testing
authors: Arghavan Moradi Dakhel, Amin Nikanjam, Vahid Majdinasab, Foutse Khomh, Michel C. Desmarais
abstract: This paper introduces MuTAP, which augments LLM prompts with surviving mutant information to iteratively improve test fault-detection. Achieves mutation score of 93.57% on synthetic buggy code; detects 28% more faulty code snippets than baseline approaches.

title: ChatUniTest: A Framework for LLM-Based Test Generation
authors: Yinghao Chen, Zehao Hu, Chen Zhi, Junxiao Han, Shuiguang Deng, Jianwei Yin
abstract: ChatUniTest is presented, an LLM-based automated unit test generation framework that incorporates an adaptive focal context mechanism to encompass valuable context in prompts and adheres to a generation-validation-repair mechanism to rectify errors in generated unit tests.

title: LLMs and Prompting for Unit Test Generation: A Large-Scale Evaluation
authors: Wendkûuni C. Ouédraogo, Kader Kabore, Haoye Tian, Yewei Song, Anil Koyuncu, Jacques Klein, David Lo, Tégawendé F. Bissyandé
venue: 2024 IEEE/ACM International Conference on Automated Software Engineering (ASE)
abstract: This study evaluates four LLMs and five prompt engineering techniques, analyzing 216 300 tests for 690 Java classes from diverse datasets to assess correctness, readability, coverage, and bug detection, comparing LLM-generated tests to EvoSuite.

title: HITS: High-Coverage LLM-Based Unit Test Generation via Method Slicing
authors: Zejun Wang, Kaibo Liu, Ge Li, Zhi Jin
venue: 2024 IEEE/ACM International Conference on Automated Software Engineering (ASE)
abstract: This work decomposes the focal methods into slices and simplifies the analysis scope, making it easier for the LLM to cover more lines and branches in each slice, and significantly outperforms current test case generation methods with LLMs and the typical SBST method Evosuite regarding both line and branch coverage scores.

title: CoverUp: Effective High Coverage Test Generation for Python
authors: Juan Altmayer Pizzorno, Emery D. Berger
venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Software Engineering (FSE 2025)
abstract: This paper proposes CoverUp, a novel approach to driving the generation of high-coverage Python regression tests that combines coverage analysis, code context, and feedback in prompts that iteratively guide the LLM to generate tests that improve line and branch coverage.

title: TestGenEval: A Real World Unit Test Generation and Test Completion Benchmark
authors: Kush Jain, Gabriel Synnaeve, Baptiste RoziÃ¨re
abstract: This work creates and releases TestGenEval, a large-scale benchmark to measure test generation performance, and evaluates several popular models, with sizes ranging from 7B to 405B parameters.

title: TestSpark: IntelliJ IDEA's Ultimate Test Generation Companion
authors: Arkadii Sapozhnikov, Mitchell Olsthoorn, Annibale Panichella, Vladimir Kovalenko, Pouria Derakhshanfar
abstract: Test-Spark is introduced, a plugin for IntelliJ IDEA that enables users to generate unit tests with only a few clicks directly within their Integrated Development Environment (IDE) and introduces a technique to generate unit tests using Large Language Models (LLMs).

title: AI-Powered Unit Test Generation via Multi-LLM Chaining: A Case Study With GPT-4o, Gemini, and Claude-3.5
authors: Chandan Kumar, Usha Sri Ponaka, P. V. L. N. Naidu, P. Bhuvaneswari, Mukesh Prasad, Sunil Kumar Singh
abstract: This paper presents a novel method, LLM Chaining, that uses the collaboration of several LLMs, namely Gemini, GPT-4o, and Claude-3.5 Sonnet, to collaborate and iteratively enhance tests to enhance the accuracy and coverage of the produced tests.

title: LLMTestCraft: An Automated Unit Test Case Generator using Large Language Models
authors: Jamal Abdullahi Nuh, T. W. Koh, Babangida Lawal, Adam Amril Jaharadak, Mohamed Ali
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Data and Software Engineering (ICoDSE)
abstract: Evaluation results across diverse Python functions demonstrate that LLMTestCraft consistently generates semantically accurate and meaningful test cases with a 92.6 % correctness rate, a significant advancement in AI-assisted software testing.

title: LLMs for Automated Unit Test Generation and Assessment in Java: The AgoneTest Framework
authors: Andrea Lops, Fedelucio Narducci, Azzurra Ragone, Michelantonio Trizio, Claudio Bart
venue: 2025 IEEE/ACM International Conference on Automated Software Engineering (ASE)
abstract: An automated evaluation framework for Large Language Model-generated unit tests in Java that clarifies the potential of LLMs in software testing and offers insights for future improvements in model design, prompt engineering, and testing practices is introduced.

title: Enhancing Automated Unit Test Generation with Large Language Models: A Systematic Literature Review
authors: Junwei Zhang, Xing Hu, Cuiyun Gao, Xin Xia, Shanping Li
venue: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology
abstract: A systematic literature review of LLM-based unit test generation reveals that Decoder-only LLMs, particularly GPT-family and LLaMA-based models, dominate the field, while encoder-only and encoder–decoder models remain underexplored.

title: Automatic Unit Test Generation for Programming Assignments Using Large Language Models
authors: Kai Zheng, Yuanyang Shen, Yida Tao
venue: 2025 IEEE/ACM International Conference on Software Engineering Education and Training
abstract: The feasibility of using Large Language Models to automate the assessment of programming assignments is explored and two approaches are proposed: the plain approach that uses GPT-4o-mini in a vanilla setting, and the augmented approach that integrates additional strategies such as tailored prompts with syntax and semantic constraints.

title: From Scenario to Code: Structured Prompting for LLM-Based Unit Test Generation
authors: Aminata Diop, Fadel Touré, Mourad Badri
venue: Proceedings of the 2025 7th World Symposium on Software Engineering
abstract: This work proposes a novel approach referred as Two-Step Zero-Shot Prompting (2SZSP), which leverages large language models (LLMs) to structure test generation by identifying relevant test scenarios and generating the corresponding unit test code.

title: An initial investigation of ChatGPT unit test generation capability
venue: 8th Brazilian Symposium on Systematic and Automated Software Testing
abstract: The findings revealed that the OpenAI LLM test set demonstrated similar performance across all evaluated aspects compared to traditional automated Java test generation tools used in the previous research.
